summary: Second wife of William Wells of Southold and later wife of Thomas Mapes Jr.; her maiden name is unknown. John's 10th-great-grandmother.
bio:
Mary, whose maiden name is unknown, is recorded as born in 1619 at Norwich in Norfolk, England. About 1654 she married William Wells of Southold on Long Island as his second wife, and after his death she married Thomas Mapes Jr. A family tradition made her a Youngs, a sister or daughter of the Rev. John Youngs of Southold, but the historian Hayes could find nothing to support it, and the Youngs family's own genealogy lists no such daughter.

Her own deed of gift of 26 December 1678, made as 'Mary Mapes of Southold, the relect of William Wells and now wife to Thomas Mapes Junr', gave property to her son-in-law John Youngs and 'Mary Yongs his wife my daughter'. The Youngs connection therefore came through her daughter's marriage, not through her own birth. A Southold record of 1677 mentions her son William Wells being taught a trade. She was still living at the end of 1678.
sources: Southold Town Records v1; WikiTree Wells-639

[R4-S1] J. Wickham Case, ed., Southold Town Records, vol. 1 (1882), pp. 302-303: deed of gift 26 Dec 1678 (recorded 3 Apr 1679) by 'Mary Mapes of Southold ... the relect of William Wells of ye sd Town ... lately desceased, and now wife to Thomas Mapes Junr', who had received all Wells's lands and goods by his deed of gift, to 'my son in law John Yongs, in right of his wife and to Mary Yongs his wife my daughter' (witnesses Thomas Mapes, William Wells); also an entry (Liber page 141, 1677) of meadow had 'of Mary Mapes formerly ye wife of Mr William Wells, in part of pay for teaching her son William his tread' (primary) https://archive.org/details/southoldtownreco0000jwic

[R4-S2] Selah Youngs Jr., Youngs Family: Vicar Christopher Yonges, his ancestors in England and his descendants in America (1907), pp. 38-41 (First and Second Generations) (secondary) https://archive.org/details/youngsfamilyvica00youn

researchNotes:
Hayes (1878, pp. 27–28): Wells married about 1654 'Mary… whose family name is said to be Youngs', adding 'Thus far I have found nothing to throw any light on the question'; she 'can hardly have been' Rev. John Youngs's sister (who married William Browne of Salem), nor his daughter Mary (b. 1631) who 'more prob. m. Edward Petty'. Her own will of 26 Dec 1678, as 'Mary Mapes … relict of William Wells', names 'my son-in-law John Youngs, in right of his wife … Mary Youngs, his wife, my daughter' — the Youngs connection came through a daughter, not the mother (as Hayes guessed). Tree: 'Mary Maria YOUNGS 1619–1709', father 'John E M o Yonges' 1598–1671.

The Southold town records print the deed of gift of 26 Dec 1678 by 'Mary Mapes of Southold ... the relect of William Wells ... and now wife to Thomas Mapes Junr' to her son-in-law John Yongs and 'Mary Yongs his wife my daughter' ([R4-S1]). This is the wife of William Wells (the tree's 'Mary Youngs'). The record shows her second husband was Thomas Mapes Jr. and that her daughter, not she, married a Youngs. A 1677 entry mentions her son William Wells being taught a trade ([R4-S1]). Her maiden name is unknown. The tree's 'daughter of Rev. John Youngs' is not supported: Youngs 1907 lists no such daughter ([R4-S2]).
